title: Corrections that did not travel
what_this_is: Cases where an organisation publicly corrected a published evaluation number, and the superseded number is still being served somewhere today. Each row carries both values, the downstream citer, what that citer serves right now, and the UTC time it was fetched.
this_is_a_mechanism_failure_not_miscondu: Every corrector here did the hard part: it found an error in its own published work and said so in public. That is rarer than it should be and it is the behaviour the field asks for. No motive is attributed to anyone. The finding is structural -- nothing binds a published number to the run that produced it, so a correction has no way to reach the places the number travelled to.
the_pattern: In 4 of the 9 cases the stale number sits on the CORRECTOR'S OWN property: ARC Prize's own R1 post, MLCommons' own machine-readable results file, METR's own Substack mirror, and NIST's own PDF. The most common shape is not downstream ignoring a correction -- it is the corrector's own surfaces disagreeing with each other.
the_machine_readable_corollary: MLCommons shows the sharpest version. The withdrawal is recorded on the change-log HTML page while summary_results.json, which is what actually feeds downstream systems, still serves the withdrawn rows unflagged. A correction published only to humans does not reach software.

verified_by_author_directly: UK AISI / OpenAI GPT-5.5 system card

verification_levels.note: Those three were re-fetched and grepped by the author against raw bytes. The remaining rows carry the fetching agent's URL and UTC timestamp and were not independently re-fetched.

did_not_travel.note: Verified directly by the author: the served document contains '1/10' and contains no '2/10' or '2 of 10' anywhere, on the web version or in the 2.37MB PDF. The document is NOT frozen -- its own change log carries entries dated 23 April, 24 April and 19 August 2026, so it was rebuilt after the correction and kept the old number. The PDF carries zero digital-signature markers.
Verified directly by the author: the page contains '$20' and '$3.4K' and contains neither '$26' nor '$4,560'. The correction did not travel one hop inside the correcting organisation's own website.

nulls.finding: No published numeric correction exists to trace. All six science pages, blog, press and antischeming.ai grepped; arXiv 2412.04984 v1 and v2 diffed and the abstracts are byte-identical including the headline figure. A null result, recorded rather than omitted.

No correction to any evaluation result exists. nist.gov/errata returns 404. Seven CAISI pages carry a later 'Updated' date with no visible change note, and with archives offline today whether a number changed is UNCHECKABLE rather than absent.

method_limitations: The Internet Archive served 'Temporarily Offline' throughout this work and archive.today timed out, so NO pre-correction value rests on an archived snapshot. Originals are established from live primary sources only.
DID_NOT_TRAVEL requires the stale value to have been SEEN in raw bytes today. 'Could not find an updated version' is UNCHECKABLE and is never recorded as a failure to travel.

Several surfaces are unreadable: ARC's leaderboard and every MLPerf results table are JavaScript shells, openai.com returns 403 to a plain client, and a GitHub issue sweep hit a rate limit after roughly 10 of 70 queries and is genuinely incomplete.

Search-engine summaries contradicted the raw bytes more than once during this work -- one asserted a GPT-5.5 correction to '3 of 10' that appears in no page actually fetched. None was used. Only strings seen in bytes are recorded here.
This is NOT a census. It is a set of confirmed instances, and the denominator is unknown: we did not establish how many published corrections exist in total, so no rate may be computed from it.
prose_count_check: The sentence above states a count that is computed, not typed. A draft of this file said 'five of the nine' while counts.stale_on_the_correctors_own_property said four. The artifact's own counter caught it before publication. Counts in prose and counts in fields must be the same count.
